query: What does emotionally unavailable actually mean?

per_question.q: Which page leaves the reader more in charge of changing this?
per_question.why: B extends the author paragraph at the end of the self-test section with 'how much of this is capacity rather than character' and 'the pull to change the subject has dropped a lot over the years, and it has not dropped to zero,' handing the reader an unfinished, self-run practice model exactly where a self-recognizing reader needs it. A's version stops at the credential dump and offers no change-model at that spot.

per_question.q: Which page asks less of the reader before it has earned it?
per_question.why: In A the identify-box contains only the reader's own sentences and their cost, with the seminar link arriving only after the box has closed; in B the link is the last line inside the box itself, so the pitch reaches the reader at the exact moment of self-recognition, before any trust is built.

per_question.q: Which page treats the reader as the person who does the work, rather than as someone who has to be sent somewhere?
per_question.why: A keeps the routing link ('How the seminar works with the distance that arrives right after a close night') outside the box where the reader is recognizing their own internal sentences; B embeds that routing inside the recognition space itself, treating the self-identifying reader as someone to redirect.

per_question.q: Which page gives the reader more room to decide for themselves what to do next?
per_question.why: B's added lines — 'people who look closed are usually people who never got fifty low-stakes repetitions' and 'I would rather tell you that than sell a finished version of something nobody finishes' — describe a self-directed option and explicitly decline to sell an outcome, leaving the next step open; A's standalone top link is also the more visually prominent nudge toward the seminar.

per_question.q: Which page puts the author's own history to better use for the reader?
per_question.why: B turns the five years / five thousand hours / fifty thousand dollars sentence into a payoff for the reader: the underestimated lesson that this is capacity not character, plus the honest present-tense admission that the pull 'has not dropped to zero.' A leaves the same history as an unconverted credential list ending in Vanuatu and Peru.

per_question.q: Which page's opening is easier to read straight through without being interrupted?
per_question.why: In B the link is absorbed as the footer of the identify-box, so the eye passes from the boxes directly into 'There is a small move most people searching this phrase already know by heart'; in A the link floats as a standalone interstitial between the box and that paragraph, an ad-slot break in the opening flow.

per_question.q: Which page makes a reader likelier to think "that is me" in the first thirty seconds?
per_question.why: The recognition beat peaks at the box's closing line about the people closest to you never finding out who is in there; A lets that line stand as the box's final note, while B immediately undercuts it with a promotional link inside the same box.

per_question.q: Which page keeps its argument moving without a detour that breaks the thread?
per_question.why: B's thread runs from the front-matter boxes straight into the 'small move' narrative that sets up everything below; A inserts an orphan seminar link between those two connected pieces, a dangling detour right where the argument is being launched.

per_question.q: Which page makes it easier to follow the line from the question at the top to the answer?
per_question.why: With the link folded into the identify-box, B's top of page reads as answer box, recognition box, then the orienting prose with no competing element; A's free-standing link between the boxes and the prose adds one off-line element the reader must step over to stay on the path.
